inputs: A CoverageReport, a trigger reference, and explicit frequency evidence
A CapabilityRegistry, for adjacency and for who provides what
invariants: A gap needs evidence and something actually missing; full active coverage cannot become a gap (rule 17).
Frequency is supplied, never inferred: recurring needs at least three counted occurrences plus pointers.
The decision table checks cheap answers first; a permanent role is the last option considered.
no_subagents on a role specification must be exactly True (rule 2).
A restricted role emits an empty may_write no matter what it requested (rule 11).
Every proposal is born PROPOSED and there is no apply(); acting on one is a human edit elsewhere.
outputs: RoleSpecification and the agent contract it emits
purpose: Turns a proven inability into a ranked recommendation and, at most, a proposed role contract. Recommends only; nothing here hires, activates or archives.
risks: requires_ceo_approval reads permissions.yaml ceo_reserved; renaming that key silently stops flagging executive hires.
Adjacency for retraining comes from registry relations, so a missing edge reads as nobody being retrainable.
title: Capability gaps, proposals and role specifications
